# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Overview

The Green Party's 2024 manifesto addresses the cost of living crisis, climate emergency, and public service decline. It proposes significant public investment funded through wealth taxation and borrowing.

## Health and Social Care

The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability for all, boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. The party opposes NHS privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill.

For social care, the manifesto proposes £20bn annual investment, free personal care, improved pay and career structures for carers, and increased disability benefits by 5%.

## Housing

The manifesto targets 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and investing £29bn over five years in home insulation. Planning reforms would protect green spaces while ensuring new developments include necessary infrastructure.

## Energy and Climate

Proposals include wind providing 70% of UK electricity by 2030, no new oil and gas licences, ending fossil fuel subsidies, and community ownership of energy sources. The manifesto calls for phasing out nuclear power and introducing a carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne, rising to £500.

## Economy and Work

The manifesto proposes £40bn average annual green investment, bringing railways, water companies, and major energy retailers into public ownership, and establishing regional mutual banks. Worker-focused policies include a £15 minimum wage, 10:1 maximum pay ratios, repealing anti-union legislation, and moving toward a four-day working week.

## Welfare

Proposals include increasing Universal Credit by £40 weekly, ending the five-week benefit wait, abolishing the two-child cap, increasing carer's allowance by 10%, and scrapping the bedroom tax.

## Public Finances

Revenue would come from a wealth tax (1% on assets above £10m, 2% above £1bn), aligning capital gains tax with income tax rates, reforming inheritance tax, and carbon taxation. The party estimates raising £50-70bn annually through tax reforms by parliament's end.

## Environment and Nature

The manifesto proposes a Rights of Nature Act, protecting 30% of land and seas by 2030, returning water companies to public ownership, and investing £1.5bn additional funding for environmental agencies. A Right to Roam Act would expand public access to green spaces.

## Education

Proposals include £8bn school investment, £2bn teacher pay uplift, £5bn for special needs provision, scrapping tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, and free school meals for all children.

## Transport

The manifesto proposes £10bn annual public transport subsidies, bringing railways into public ownership, £2.5bn annually for cycling and walking infrastructure, free bus travel for under-18s, and ending petrol and diesel vehicle sales by 2027.

## Democracy and Rights

Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post with proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, defending the Human Rights Act, and repealing recent protest restrictions.

## Immigration

The manifesto calls for ending the hostile environment, establishing safe asylum routes, ending minimum income requirements for spousal visas, and allowing asylum seekers to work during application processing.

## Foreign Policy

Key positions include supporting an immediate bilateral ceasefire in Gaza, recognising Palestine, ending UK arms exports to Israel, rejoining the EU, signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, and increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI.

## Funding

The statistical appendix shows revenue spending rising from £99.2bn in 2025-26 to £161.6bn by 2029-30, with capital spending rising from £22.8bn to £90.3bn. Taxation revenue would increase from £36.7bn to £172.4bn, with remaining deficits funded through borrowing.
